For DEUTZ, the core belief is that the shift from traditional engines toward a more diversified mix across Services, Energy, Defense and NewTech can support earnings even when legacy engine demand is soft. The latest nine month figures show higher sales and net income, which supports that transition story but does not change the need for disciplined integration and cost control in the near term.

The key short term swing factor remains how effectively DEUTZ turns its newer divisions into consistent profit pools while engine volumes stay under pressure. Balance sheet risk still matters, with higher leverage and financing costs a live issue. If cash generation lags, that becomes the biggest near term operational risk.

Management previously highlighted €37 million of additional Energy revenue in the first half of 2026 and a €220 million backlog, alongside an internal ambition for materially higher revenue over time. The latest nine month profit picture arrives against that backdrop of heavier investment and scaling efforts.

For you as a shareholder or potential shareholder, the link is straightforward. Execution on integration, order conversion and cash collection in this unit will influence how comfortable investors feel with the higher debt load and with treating the recent EPS improvement as repeatable rather than one off.

DEUTZ's current earnings of €78.7 million are set against analyst forecasts for €301.0 million of profit and €4.2 billion of revenue by 2029, which implies revenue growth of 25.1% per year and an earnings increase of roughly 3.8x from today into that 2029 estimate year.

data.title: There May Be Underlying Issues With The Quality Of Eleganz Interiors' (NSE:ELGNZ) Earnings
data.description:
Investors were disappointed with Eleganz Interiors Limited's (NSE:ELGNZ) earnings, despite the strong profit numbers. Our analysis uncovered some concerning factors that we believe the market might be paying attention to.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

Zooming In On Eleganz Interiors' Earnings

In high finance, the key ratio used to measure how well a company converts reported profits into free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio (from cashflow). The accrual ratio subtracts the FCF from the profit for a given period, and divides the result by the average operating assets of the company over that time. This ratio tells us how much of a company's profit is not backed by free cashflow.

Therefore, it's actually considered a good thing when a company has a negative accrual ratio, but a bad thing if its accrual ratio is positive. While it's not a problem to have a positive accrual ratio, indicating a certain level of non-cash profits, a high accrual ratio is arguably a bad thing, because it indicates paper profits are not matched by cash flow. That's because some academic studies have suggested that high accruals ratios tend to lead to lower profit or less profit growth.

Over the twelve months to September 2026, Eleganz Interiors recorded an accrual ratio of 0.38. As a general rule, that bodes poorly for future profitability. And indeed, during the period the company didn't produce any free cash flow whatsoever. Even though it reported a profit of ₹268.6m, a look at free cash flow indicates it actually burnt through ₹434m in the last year. Coming off the back of negative free cash flow last year, we imagine some shareholders might wonder if its cash burn of ₹434m, this year, indicates high risk.

Our Take On Eleganz Interiors' Profit Performance

As we discussed above, we think Eleganz Interiors' earnings were not supported by free cash flow, which might concern some investors. For this reason, we think that Eleganz Interiors' statutory profits may be a bad guide to its underlying earnings power, and might give investors an overly positive impression of the company. But the happy news is that, while acknowledging we have to look beyond the statutory numbers, those numbers are still improving, with EPS growing at a very high rate over the last year. Of course, we've only just scratched the surface when it comes to analysing its earnings; one could also consider margins, forecast growth, and return on investment, among other factors. data.title: Vertiv Holdings Co (VRT) Faces Fresh Regulatory Pressure On AI Data Center Buildouts
data.description:
• Vertiv Holdings Co (NYSE:VRT) faces fresh scrutiny after a recent Democratic sweep in key US elections raised policy risks for AI data center projects.
  • Following those results, several Democratic lawmakers have publicly backed tighter environmental reviews and zoning limits for large scale AI computing hubs in multiple states.
  • In Texas, new discussions around grid reliability and water usage standards for power hungry AI facilities are prompting concerns about slower data center permitting timelines.
  • These political and regulatory pressures on US AI data center build outs could reshape expectations for Vertiv's infrastructure pipeline, although the business story extends beyond the new permitting and policy headwinds. We have also flagged 1 warning sign for Vertiv Holdings Co.

Readers looking for more ideas linked to this AI build out theme often widen the lens to 52 AI infrastructure stocks.

Vertiv Holdings Co provides power management, cooling equipment, and life cycle services for data centers and communication networks worldwide, putting its US$68.1 billion electrical business close to the front line of any policy shifts that affect large AI computing sites.

See how Vertiv Holdings Co's balance sheet measures up.

How new AI permitting risks test Vertiv’s AI build-out Narrative

The Vertiv Holdings Co Narrative assumes AI-driven data center projects keep scaling quickly enough that complex power and cooling systems like SmartRun and OneCore stay busy and profitable, even as projects get denser and more technically demanding.

"The main thing that has to go right is consistent execution on complex SmartRun, OneCore and large infrastructure projects so that growing system complexity, supply chain congestion and the learning curve on multidimensional solutions do not erode the strong profitability now visible in recent quarters..."

See how the full story points towards a $338 fair value for Vertiv Holdings Co.

The new push from Democratic policymakers for tighter environmental reviews and stricter zoning directly leans on one of the Narrative’s key supports: a fast moving AI project pipeline that justifies Vertiv’s higher long term organic growth target. Slower permitting for US data centers, especially in power constrained states like Texas, could stretch project timelines and make those complex SmartRun and OneCore deployments lumpy. That is the same kind of timing risk analysts have already flagged after earlier multiphase project shifts.

On the other hand, these policy debates speak less to demand for Vertiv’s hardware and more to the pace and location of that demand. This ties back to risks around supply chain reconfiguration and EMEA execution rather than the overall AI thesis. If US permitting tightens, the AI infrastructure spend may skew further to regions where Vertiv already supplies liquid cooling and 800V DC projects alongside rivals such as Eaton and Schneider Electric, keeping the focus on whether the firm can keep margins intact when complexity rises.

That framework also assumes a payout ratio around 50% to 55% of free cash flow and almost no net debt, while deliberately leaving buybacks out of the equation to keep the estimate on the conservative side.

Under that lens, the recent rally in Automatic Data Processing pushes the share price meaningfully above this narrative fair value, which suggests investors are currently paying up for qualities such as recurring revenue, high reported return on equity, and a long dividend track record rather than buying primarily on a discount to intrinsic worth.
